ran: drove createRestrictedDb with an extension holding no grants: selectFrom('session') and selectFrom('zv_api_keys') refused, while sql`SELECT token FROM session`, sql`SELECT id FROM zv_api_keys`, sql`SELECT token FROM zv_invitations` and sql`UPDATE "user" SET role='god'` all went through.
instrumented a proxy to log every property a raw sql template touches on the handle: exactly one, `getExecutor`. A first guard on `executeQuery` changed nothing, which is how that was found.

wrote the guard, confirmed all four escapes refused and that builder queries, explicitly granted tables, own-namespace tables, CTEs, joins, insert+returning and interpolated sql fragments all still pass.
ran assertWorkerSqlAllowed over all 1170 raw statements the first-party extensions ship: 18 extensions reference tables outside their own namespace, most of them legitimately.
the same scan found the policy refusing `lateral`, `now`, `date`, `start_date` and `invoice_date` — none of them tables. Fixed in #457.
measured zv_invitations: no RLS, no policy, tenant_id present, and zveltio_rls holds SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on it.
corrected an environment mistake that had been reported all day as a pre-existing test failure: the harness needs NODE_ENV=test, which CI sets. With it the suite is 1072 pass / 0 fail, not 1071/1.

findings.what: the table allowlist guards the query-builder entry points only; a raw `sql` template reaches the database through getExecutor and is unchecked. An extension with no grants read session.token and zv_api_keys and ran UPDATE "user" SET role='god'. The fix is written and measured but refuses 18 first-party extensions that use the path legitimately, so it is an owner decision about grants rather than a repair.

invitation tokens stored in plaintext in a table with no RLS and no policy, while the same codebase hashes reset, verification and recovery tokens with an argument that applies here verbatim. Not reachable through the API today — there is no listing endpoint.

the legacy scrypt branch compares the derived key with `!==` while the rest of the codebase uses constant-time comparison for secrets. No practical oracle — the attacker supplies the password, not the digest.
read `LATERAL`, function calls after FROM, and EXTRACT/TRIM/SUBSTRING keyword arguments as table names, refusing ordinary first-party SQL and naming tables that do not exist.

notDone: PARTIAL. lib/auth.ts read at the parts that decide identity — the registration chokepoint, password hashing and verification, the session and cookie configuration — but not end to end. keyring.ts read at its structure only. routes/users.ts read at the invitation endpoints only. The raw-SQL finding took the session's remaining time, and it is worth more than the line count it cost.
